restaurantLevelAllergenEvidence.text: Chick-fil-A says shared cooking and preparation areas and supplier variation mean it cannot ensure food is free from allergens; wheat, egg, soy, and milk products are made in its kitchens. This is retained at restaurant level and not expanded into unsupported item-specific may-contain claims.

Chick-fil-A states its hand-breaded chicken is cooked in fully refined peanut oil and that highly refined peanut oil is not considered a major food allergen; no peanut positive is inferred from the cooking oil.

evidence.excerpt: Live official nutrition/allergen system contained 174 top-level rows in 17 sections, consolidated to 162 unique current products. Contains flags cover milk, egg, soy, wheat, sesame, tree nuts, peanut, and fish.
Official Chick-fil-A homepage identifies the national chain and currently promotes Honey Pepper Pimento, Peach treats, Pineapple Dragonfruit beverages, and the Mac & Cheese Kid?s Meal.
Official national menu landing page covering breakfast, entr?es, salads, sides, beverages, treats, Kid?s Meals, Family Style Meals, and catering; price and availability may vary by location.

Official FAQ says fully refined peanut oil is not considered a major allergen, but shared cooking/preparation areas and supplier variation mean food cannot be ensured allergen-free; wheat, egg, soy, and milk products are made in Chick-fil-A kitchens.
